Farming is very important to the lifeblood of this nation. These morons, idiots, ratbags—you name it—are the ones who are actually going out protesting and trespassing, and they think they're doing a wonderful job in trying to help the animals, but, as I expressed here in my speech before, they are actually killing animals. They are actually seeing the death of animals, as I have explained. Farming is a life of dedication, effort and hardship. As we know, it is a struggle for farmers to make good profits year in and year out. A relatively small number of people here in the parliament would have a deep understanding of rural living and life on the land—a very small number. I'd like to really have an understanding of how many people, especially Greens, who are actually standing up and making comments, have ever lived on a rural property, bred livestock, understand drought and understand the connection with the livestock that you rear. Very few in this chamber have ever experienced that—very few. You need to understand the commitment and the hardships that are connected with this. You do look after your animals, but, at the end of the day, you rear animals as part of the food chain. They are there for us to eat, to consume, to sell. That's what these animals are reared for. If you have a pet sheep, fine; that's your pet. Don't start imposing your views, your thoughts, on the businesses in the farming sector. They have businesses for their own livelihoods and income. The Criminal Code Amendment (Agricultural Protection) Bill 2019 introduces new offences for using a carriage service to incite trespass, property damage, destruction or theft on agricultural land, with penalties of up to 12 months imprisonment for inciting trespass and up to five years for inciting damage or theft. The bill includes exemptions for journalists and whistleblowers, and builds on earlier action to prescribe the Aussie Farms website under the Privacy Act, exposing it to potential penalties of up to $2.1 million.

Labor argued the bill may be unnecessary due to existing state and territory laws already criminalising trespass, property damage and theft, and raised concerns it could infringe on democratic rights, whistleblower protections, journalism, native title access and legitimate industrial action. Labor will not oppose the bill in the House but will await the Senate Legal and Constitutional Affairs Legislation Committee's report before announcing a final position.

The Criminal Code Amendment (Agricultural Protection) Bill 2019 is a necessary response to online incitement of trespass and property offences against farmers, and the bill was commended to the House.
